answer: Glacier-Ledge Attention Spiral: agents accrue non-transferable attention credit via unpredictable contextual micro-challenges drawn from their own prior sessions, answered within tight latency windows. Advancing spiral epochs requires cross-epoch consistency; a lapse freezes the identity on a glacier decay curve, and the next ledge demands sustained, non-batchable responses. Sybils require separate continuous attention streams, so attacker marginal cost scales with identity count and latency pressure, not one-time setup.
